newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOBIL, JAPAN FIRMS QUIT VIET BLUE DRAGON OIL FIELD.
newsitem.headline: MOBIL, JAPAN FIRMS QUIT VIET BLUE DRAGON OIL FIELD.

text.p: A consortium comprised of Mobil Corp of the United States and four Japanese oil firms has pulled the plug on development of the Thanh Long oil and gas field off Vietnam, a spokesman for the state-run Japan National Oil Company (JNOC) said on Thursday.
The move follows three years of fruitless drilling and exploration, the spokesman said.
The consortium, known as MJC, is made up of Mobil, which has a 45 percent stake, as well as JNOC, Indonesia Petroleum Ltd, Japan Petroleum Exploration, and Nissho Iwai Corp.
MJC Petroleum has a 72.5 percent holding in the Thanh Long field, which was discovered by Mobil in 1975 and is also known as the Blue Dragon field.
MJC's partners in the project are Vietnam state oil agency PetroVietnam, and Russia's Zarubezhneft.
"The operator, MJC, conducted a feasibility study ending in July which has shown that the field, economically, is not good," the spokesman said
The JNOC spokesman said the consortium's exploration contract was good until October, but that there would be no further drilling.
"It has been shown that the field's oil and gas reserves do not warrant commercial development," the spokesman said.
